## Introduction

This project looks at whether I spend more time on my phone during weekdays or weekends. I recorded my screen time for 21 consecutive days, from October 19 through November 8, 2026.

## Research Question and Hypotheses

**Research question:** Is my average daily screen time different between weekdays and weekends?

**Null hypothesis (H0):** Average daily screen time is the same on weekdays and weekends.

**Alternative hypothesis (Ha):** Average daily screen time is different on weekdays and weekends.

## Import and Clean Data

```{r, message=FALSE}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

ScreenTime <- read_excel("TranScreenTimeDataLog.xlsx", skip = 3)
names(ScreenTime) <- c("Date", "Day", "DayType", "ScreenTime")

# Convert hours and minutes into total minutes.
ScreenTime <- ScreenTime %>%
  filter(!is.na(ScreenTime)) %>%
  mutate(
    Hours = as.numeric(sub("h.*", "", ScreenTime)),
    MinutePart = trimws(sub(".*h", "", ScreenTime)),
    MinutePart = ifelse(MinutePart == "", "0", MinutePart),
    Minutes = as.numeric(gsub("m", "", MinutePart)),
    TotalMinutes = Hours * 60 + Minutes,
    Date = as.Date(Date),
    DayType = factor(DayType, levels = c("Weekday", "Weekend"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(Date)

ScreenTime %>% select(Date, Day, DayType, TotalMinutes)
```

## Summary Statistics

```{r}
SummaryStats <- ScreenTime %>%
  group_by(DayType) %>%
  summarize(
    Days = n(),
    Mean = round(mean(TotalMinutes), 2),
    SD = round(sd(TotalMinutes), 2),
    Minimum = min(TotalMinutes),
    Maximum = max(TotalMinutes),
    Range = max(TotalMinutes) - min(TotalMinutes)
  )

knitr::kable(SummaryStats, caption = "Screen Time Summary Statistics (Minutes)")
```

## Graph 1: Screen Time by Day Type (Boxplot)

This is the same boxplot shown on my research poster. Navy represents weekdays and teal represents weekends. The yellow diamonds show the group averages.

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=5, echo=TRUE}
ggplot(ScreenTime, aes(x = DayType, y = TotalMinutes, fill = DayType)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, color = "#627382") +
  geom_point(data = SummaryStats,
             aes(x = DayType, y = Mean),
             inherit.aes = FALSE,
             shape = 18, size = 4, color = "#E6AD43") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Weekday" = "#1D3858",
                               "Weekend" = "#15818D")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Weekdays (15)", "Weekends (6)")) +
  labs(
    title = "Screen Time by Day Type",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Screen time (minutes)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

### Interpretation

The boxplot shows how my screen time varies between weekdays and weekends. Weekday screen time was generally higher, although the groups overlap.

## Graph 2: Average Daily Screen Time (Bar Graph)

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=5, echo=TRUE}
AverageTime <- ScreenTime %>%
  group_by(DayType) %>%
  summarize(AverageMinutes = mean(TotalMinutes))

ggplot(AverageTime, aes(x = DayType, y = AverageMinutes, fill = DayType)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.60) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste(round(AverageMinutes, 1), "min")),
            vjust = -0.4, fontface = "bold", size = 5, color = "#1D3858") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Weekday" = "#1D3858",
                               "Weekend" = "#15818D")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Weekdays\n(n=15)", "Weekends\n(n=6)")) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Daily Screen Time",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Average screen time (minutes)"
  ) +
  ylim(0, 560) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

### Interpretation

The weekday average was 467.67 minutes, while the weekend average was 331.00 minutes. This is a difference of 136.67 minutes, or about 2 hours and 17 minutes per day.

## Graph 3: Screen Time Over 21 Days (Line Graph)

The teal points highlight weekend observations, like on my research poster.

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=5, echo=TRUE}
ggplot(ScreenTime, aes(x = Date, y = TotalMinutes)) +
  geom_line(color = "#1D3858", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "#1D3858", size = 2.5) +
  geom_point(data = filter(ScreenTime, DayType == "Weekend"),
             aes(color = "Weekend"), size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Weekend" = "#15818D")) +
  labs(
    title = "Screen Time Over 21 Days",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Screen time (minutes)",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  ylim(150, 650) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

### Interpretation

My screen time changed from day to day. Many of my lower screen-time days were on weekends.

## Graph 4: Distribution of Daily Screen Time (Histogram)

This fourth graph is included in my R Markdown report to meet the course requirement. My poster features the other three graphs.

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=5, echo=TRUE}
ggplot(ScreenTime, aes(x = TotalMinutes)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 60, fill = "#1D3858", color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Daily Screen Time",
    x = "Screen time (minutes)",
    y = "Number of days"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

### Interpretation

The histogram shows how often different amounts of daily screen time occurred during the study.

## Statistical Analysis: Two-Sample t-Test

I used a Welch two-sample t-test to compare the weekday and weekend averages.

```{r}
ScreenTimeTest <- t.test(TotalMinutes ~ DayType, data = ScreenTime)
ScreenTimeTest
```

### Interpretation

My average screen time was **467.67 minutes on weekdays** and **331.00 minutes on weekends**. The Welch two-sample t-test had a **p-value of approximately 0.0061**. Since this is less than 0.05, I reject the null hypothesis. My data show a statistically significant difference between weekday and weekend screen time.

## Conclusion and Limitations

During these three weeks, I spent more time on my phone on weekdays than weekends. The results reflect my own phone use for only 21 days, including six weekend days. Because I recorded consecutive days from one person, the observations may not be fully independent. These results cannot be generalized to everyone, and they do not explain why the difference occurred.
